title: cost-optimization: autotune batching/caching defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Anjali Rao
description: Motivation: Reduce per-token inference cost across hosted and dedicated deployments by providing sane autotuned defaults for batching/caching, adding model quantization profiles, and exposing unit-economics tooling so operators can see the expected cost impact of config changes. This PR implements three coordinated workstreams: (1) autotune defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching that adapt to observed latency/throughput signals, (2) a first pass at named quantization profiles (fp16/int8/awq variants) with compatibility metadata for the runtime and routing layer, and (3) server + console unit-economics APIs and dashboard components that surface per-request and per-route token cost estimates and recommend presets. The description below summarizes changes, testing, rollout, and follow-ups. Changes: - Runtime/autotune: added a new autotuner that picks default batch_size, max_latency_ms, and cache_policy per-model-per-route based on short-window traffic stats; falls back to global defaults if insufficient data. Tuners are lightweight (CPU-only control loop) and emit metrics for auditing. - Batching/cache defaults: introduced new config files and feature flags (autotune_enabled, autotune_sampling_window) and a deterministic migration for existing customers to opt into recommended defaults. - Quantization profiles: added model metadata schema for quant_profiles with compatibility flags (supported_kernels, expected_mem_savings, approx_quality_impact). The model registry exposes profiles so the router can fallback to a compatible profile when the preferred profile is unavailable. - Unit economics tooling: server API /v1/internal/unit_econ that returns per-route per-model cost projections and recommended quant/batch/cache presets. Console dashboard component (UnitEconDashboard) displays cost breakdowns, projected monthly savings, and a 1-click apply button that creates a rollout for the recommended preset. - Observability: new metrics (autotune.recommendation.count, autotune.applied.count, unit_econ.estimate.ms) and Grafana dashboard panels. - Tests & CI: unit tests for tuner logic and integration tests simulating traffic profiles; perf canary added to perf-canary suite. Rollout plan: 1) Feature-flagged in main for internal canary (redwood-internal) 2) Gradual opt-in for beta customers via console rollout plan with monitoring hooks 3) Full default change after 4 weeks of telemetry if error/latency budgets stable Backwards compatibility & safety: defaults are opt-in behind feature flag; quant profiles include a safe "no_quality_regressions" flag for models where we validated minimal quality impact. The autotuner never raises batch_size above a conservative upper bound per-model and always respects latency SLOs. Checklist: - [x] Autotune control loop + unit tests - [x] Quantization profile schema + registry integration - [x] Unit economics API + console UI - [x] Metrics and dashboard panels - [x] Integration & perf tests - [x] Docs (docs/cost-optimization.md) Related work: Linear ENG-2104 (autotune infrastructure), ENG-2177 (unit economics dashboard).
